# Safe to Stay Invested? Decoding 2025 Stock Charts

First listed: 2025-06-09 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Safe to Stay Invested? Decoding 2025 Stock Charts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ns7oJA4t-44) - 2025-06-09
- [Substack: Safe to Stay Invested? Decoding 2025 Stock Charts](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/safe-to-stay-invested-decoding-2025-fa3) - 2025-06-09

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Todd Sohn teaches trend, breadth, sentiment and relative-strength analysis, revises an earlier bear-market interpretation and remains constructive after the April rebound. His bullish market direction gained support, but proprietary backtests and most stock-level chart rankings lack reproducible tests. Eisman challenges false bottoms and draws attention to concentration and active-manager constraints. Long-duration caution, gold optimism and Bitcoin risk behavior are distinct views, not interchangeable diversification claims.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

- [How Has Treasury Market Liquidity Fared in 2025?](https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2025/11/how-has-treasury-market-liquidity-fared-in-2025/) (2025-11-12): Treasury volatility and illiquidity spiked around April tariffs, then quickly declined; late-summer depth and price impact recovered. ## Framework and tools

- Chart patterns are conditional clues rather than substitutes for fundamentals.
- Look through headline indices and fund names to constituent breadth and overlapping exposures.
- Separate price direction from inferred investor motives.
- A risk-management threshold is not an unconditional price forecast.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- 50-/200-day moving averages
- One-month new-high breadth and 3/6/12-month backtests
- Cap-weight versus equal-weight indices
- Discretionary/staples and high-/low-beta ratios
- ETF flow dashboard, VIX, put/call ratios and leveraged long/short AUM
- Long-duration returns after first Fed cuts

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Todd Sohn. Most technical judgments belong to Sohn. Eisman asks questions and occasionally endorses or restates a proposition; those substantive adoptions are recorded separately.
- Todd Sone/S is normalized to Todd Sohn.
- Caption 500 are 2% at 955 seconds is inconsistent with 500 equal weights; arithmetic 0.2%, flagged as supporting issue.
- Charts referenced in video were not independently supplied as underlying data; no claim that proprietary backtests were reproduced.
- Record date is inferred earlier than June 9 publication; references to nearly 40 sessions since April 8 and latest NVIDIA earnings narrow but do not fix it.
- Opening montage duplicates later discussion.
